events.credibility_reason: The 2.32 upper bound exists only as a seminar abstract; no written argument for it was found, including in Baek's later preprints.
The 2.3337 five-angle figure reads as a numerical estimate rather than a certified bound; the paper presents itself as evidence, not proof.

No named human has verified it after ~22 months; the author concedes a connectedness gap in Gerver's balancing argument; an AI audit reports a false direction of Prop. 5.1.4 and a misreading of Gerver's Theorem 2 underlying Thm 6.1.2, which the formalisers say they repaired without the main theorem breaking. These are doubts but not unanswered errors, so it is not knocked down.
The sofa section was never read; the content comes only from a search snippet. As reported, it recovers known planar shapes and adds a 3D analogue, which is a different question.
The arguments are AI-written and checked only by Lean; the README says no person has reviewed the proofs, statements or definitions.
events.ai_basis: ChatGPT Pro 6 wrote the arguments for uniqueness, stability and the certificate for this repository; they have not been peer reviewed.

events.credibility_reason: The arXiv identifier and the submission date disagree, and the results are numerical only.

why: The statement asks only for the maximal area. Baek's preprint determines that value (Gerver's sofa attains it), so its scope is whole and Gerver's sofa is a witness. Its verification is unreviewed: no named human has read it, the formal-conjectures tag cites it without checking it, and three Lean builds plus an AI audit and an AI referee are formal or automated checks, not digestion (F7, F8). I marked it doubtful rather than credible because of the author's own admitted gap and the audit's specific errors. Those errors are reported repaired, so it is not knocked down. The three formalisations are scope none with ai_role none, because the AI only formalised and audited an argument a human had already proved. The vltanh uniqueness/stability event is a stronger form of the question, so it is a variant. Its 'coercive certificate' is said to reprove optimality, but it sits inside Baek's framework, has no human reading, and the record cannot show it is an independent answer. Its AI role is generated (ChatGPT Pro 6 wrote the arguments), but that credit belongs to the variant event only. Baek's 2024-06 bound is conditional on an unproven injectivity conjecture, so it is a reduction and scored none. Leng et al. is numerical evidence with an uncertified bound, so none. Hammersley, Gerver and Kallus-Romik are pre-snapshot bounds. Romik 2016's closed form answers the ambidextrous variant.
doubts: Close call: whether the vltanh 'coercive certificate' is a second, AI-generated whole answer to the value. If it is, it would tie Baek at the top tier and pass an AI 'generated' role to the problem. I read it as a variant/extension because the record describes it only through the README and it relies on Baek's framework. Baek's own 2.32 talk bound has no written argument. The AlphaEvolve sofa section was never read.
